turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Good morning, you're through to Acme Life, my name's Mia. Just so you know, this call is recorded for quality and training purposes. How can I help you today?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Hi, yeah, um, I saw your ad on Facebook for life cover and I filled in the form for a call back, so I'm just returning the call, I think.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Lovely, thanks for calling back. Before we go into anything, can I please confirm your full name and date of birth?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Chloe Patel. Fourteenth of March, 1987.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks Chloe, that matches what I've got here. So tell me a bit about yourself and what's got you thinking about life cover.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Well, it's a bit of a weird time to be honest. I got made redundant two weeks ago, so things are pretty rough. I've got my daughter, she's six, and it's just me. Money's really tight right now, like, I'm counting every dollar. But that's sort of why I started thinking about it, if something happened to me, she'd have nothing.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Okay, so single parent, one daughter aged six, and you want something in place for her. Do you have any existing life cover, maybe through super?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I honestly don't know. I think there was something through my old job's super but I haven't looked. I've had so much going on, I can barely keep track of the bills.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: No worries. Any mortgage or major debts?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I rent. There's a car loan, about twelve thousand left on it. And a credit card I've been leaning on a bit since, you know, since the job.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Got it. Before I go through the product, I do need to let you know that anything I tell you today is general advice only. It doesn't take into account your personal objectives, financial situation or needs, so you should think about whether it's right for you. Okay, so Acme Life Cover pays a lump sum if you pass away. You can choose a cover amount anywhere from fifty thousand up to one million dollars. There's no medical exam, it's just a few health questions, and that decides whether you're accepted.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Okay. Sorry, a lump sum to who, my daughter?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: To whoever you nominate as beneficiary, or your estate. A couple of important things: in the first twelve months, only accidental death is covered. After that, you're covered for death from any cause. And the premiums are stepped, which means they go up each year as you get older.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Right... they go up. Okay. Sorry, my head's all over the place at the moment, I've been on the phone to Centrelink all morning.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Sure. So, let's run through the health questions and then I can give you a quote. Have you smoked any tobacco in the last twelve months?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with cancer, heart disease, stroke or diabetes?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, none of those.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: In the last five years, have you been advised by a doctor to have any tests or treatment that are still outstanding?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Um, no. I've been a bit stressed, not sleeping, but nothing like that.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Okay, and do you take part in any hazardous activities, like motor racing or skydiving?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Ha, no. I can barely afford petrol.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Great, so based on those answers you'd be accepted. Now cover amount, a lot of people with young kids look at around two hundred and fifty thousand. At that level, your premium would be fifty-four dollars a month to start.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Fifty-four a month. Hmm. That's... I mean, that's a fair bit for me right now. I've only got my last pay and a bit of leave money and that's got to stretch until I find something.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: You can go lower, the minimum is fifty thousand, which would bring the premium down, or higher if you want more. Two fifty is a common choice for parents.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I just keep thinking if something happened, fifty thousand wouldn't really last her. But I don't know if I can do fifty-four. I don't really get how the going up thing works either.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: So with stepped premiums, the price is recalculated each year based on your age, so it increases each year. The fifty-four is what you'd pay now. It's completely your decision, there's no pressure to do anything today, the quote's here if you want to think about it.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yeah... no, I think I just want it sorted. It's one less thing to worry about. If I wait I'll just forget about it with everything else.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Okay. Also worth knowing, there's a thirty-day cooling-off period, so if you change your mind within thirty days you can cancel and get a full refund.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Oh, okay. That helps a bit.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Right, so let me summarise. Acme Life Cover, two hundred and fifty thousand dollars, paid as a lump sum on your death. For the first twelve months, only accidental death is covered, after that it's death from any cause. Your premium is fifty-four dollars a month, and it's stepped, so it'll go up each year as you get older. You've got a thirty-day cooling-off period with a full refund. Would you like to go ahead with that?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Um... yes. Yes, I'll go ahead.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Great. And who would you like as the beneficiary?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: My daughter, Aanya Patel. Or, well, I guess my sister would have to look after it for her. Priya Patel.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: I'll note your sister Priya as beneficiary for now, and you'll get a form with your documents to update or add a trust arrangement. Now for payment, is that going to be a debit card or bank account?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Bank account, I suppose. Can it come out after the fifteenth? That's when my leave payout's meant to land.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Yes, I'll set the first debit for the sixteenth. Can you read me the BSB and account number?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: BSB is 062-415, account 1083 7726.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks, that's all set up. Your policy documents will be emailed through today, including the Product Disclosure Statement, and your thirty-day cooling-off starts from when you receive them. Anything else I can help with?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, I think that's it. Thanks.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks Chloe, have a lovely day.
